R0170.title: MEV Attacks (Miner Extractable Value)
R0170.definition: Miners or validators extracting additional value by reordering, inserting, or censoring transactions, harming ordinary user interests.
R0170.description: MEV (Miner/Maximal Extractable Value) refers to the additional profit miners/validators gain by controlling the order of transactions within blocks. Common tactics include: front-running, sandwich attacks, and arbitrage transaction reordering. When users' transactions are maliciously reordered, they may suffer slippage losses, transaction failures, or be forced to settle at unfavorable prices.
R0170.influence: Increased user transaction costs, price slippage losses, blockchain fairness compromised.

observables: User transactions are front- or back-inserted with arbitrage transactions in the pending pool, forming a sandwich attack structure
Highly correlated transaction sequences appear within the same block, with arbitrageur transactions packaged immediately following victim transactions
The actual execution price of a user transaction shows anomalous slippage deviation from the expected price at submission
Arbitrage bot addresses repeatedly execute front-running and arbitrage at high frequency across DeFi protocols
